summary: BA Path A+ scoping verified across all 5 dimensions; codex-refined hybrid is structurally sound and cycle-7 systemic-lesson cross-validation is encoded as binding AC4. One minor AC4 literal-text drift on spawn-end empty-receiver case (E3 errored-spawn) noted as advisory non-blocking objection.

objections.issue: AC4 literal text says 'if the type is spawnAgent end, receiverThreadIds is a single-element array AND agentsStates is a single-key object whose key matches receiverThreadIds[0]'. This would FAIL the legitimate errored-spawn case from event_mapping.rs:113 where new_thread_id: None yields receiver_thread_ids: Vec::new() and agents_states: HashMap::new() on spawn-end.
objections.evidence: /tmp/codex-src/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:104-114 — match end_event.new_thread_id { Some(id) => (vec![receiver_id.clone()], [(receiver_id, received_status)].into_iter().collect()), None => (Vec::new(), HashMap::new()) }
objections.recommendation: Refine AC4 wording to: 'if the type is spawnAgent end with status=completed (new_thread_id Some), receiverThreadIds is a single-element array AND agentsStates is a single-key object whose key matches receiverThreadIds[0]; if the type is spawnAgent end with status=failed/errored (new_thread_id None), receiverThreadIds is empty AND agentsStates is empty.' This aligns AC4 with the actual two-arm shape of CollabAgentSpawnEnd. Note: BA did acknowledge this case in E3 as a Dev hint — the issue is purely AC4 literal text not matching the documented shape, not a scope or design gap.
objections.non_blocking_rationale: E3 already documents the empty-receiver spawn-end case as Dev-implementation guidance (M2). The AC4 literal-text drift is a small fixture-quality gate issue, not a scope or design gap. Cycle 8 dev/QA can ignore this AC4 corner-case in fixtures (no fixture needs to exercise the errored-spawn case) and the cycle-8 fix would still close the production gap. Recommendation is for BA to refine AC4 in a future ticket revision; cycle 8 is not blocked.

investigation_completeness.notes: BA investigated Codex's own arm structure in event_mapping.rs. Critical observation: Codex's wait/close arms (lines 181-204 CollabWaitingBegin, 205+ CollabWaitingEnd) DO populate receiver_thread_ids; only the spawn-begin arm (75-86) emits empty receiverThreadIds. This means a hybrid join-key strategy is REQUIRED — pure receiverThreadId keying fails at spawn-begin; pure tool_call_id keying would lose the wait/close→spawn linkage. Path A+ correctly bridges by allocating provisional ssn at spawn-begin keyed on call_id, and binding receiverThreadId→ssn at spawn-end so subsequent wait/close events (which arrive with populated receiverThreadIds) can resolve to the same ssn. BA's 5-point Codex consult log shows substantive engagement: refinement #1 (end-side resolution requirement), #2 (call-id pairing/provisional ssn at begin — the core Path A+ insight), #3 (idempotency reliance), #4 (agentNickname null acceptance), #5 (Path B/C rejection). All 5 incorporated into MoSCoW + AC + W-list.
